_what_this_is: The GOLDEN aws-design.json for the azure-iac-terraform corpus. Pass 1 (the disposition table) AND pass 2 (compute.md + database.md) both applied. It is STILL a halted design, and the directory name says so: the corpus carries an untranslated cost-bearing type (azurerm_iothub), which STOPs Design unconditionally. That is now the ONLY blocker — the missing-rubric blockers are gone as of build step 5. Sizes carry sizing_provenance; two were corrected on 2026-09-07 when the knowledge/design sizing tables landed and contradicted them (S1 -> t3.small, GP_Standard_D2s_v3 -> db.m6g.large). Both had been model priors.
_absent_on_purpose: clusters[] carries pattern_status 'catalog_absent' because design-refs/patterns.md does not exist yet; the asserter checks only pattern_status and the target_architecture-is-null rule. Sizing numbers are dev-tier defaults stated as such: the knowledge/design/*-sizing.json tables are not on disk, and a missing SIZING table degrades a number's precision whereas a missing RUBRIC file would cost the service choice, which is why only the latter halts.

services.rationale: Direct Mappings row, condition Always. A VNet is a VPC regardless of what runs in it; the address space is preserved.
Direct Mappings row, condition Always. Node sizing is post-selection and does not revisit the service choice.

aws_config.kms_reason: no vaults/keys child and no key operations recorded in the inventory

services.rationale: Direct Mappings row, condition Always. KMS is added only when the vault holds keys; ACM for certificates. Additive company does not change the row's target.

aws_config.cloudfront_note: the static_website block adds CloudFront at the pattern layer; that is additive and does not change this row's target

services.rationale: Direct Mappings row. The condition holds because account_kind is StorageV2, not FileStorage, so the account has a blob surface. Its fileServices/shares child is mapped separately and does NOT inherit S3.

Direct Mappings row, condition enabled_protocol == SMB. Protocol is the whole rubric (owner decision 11.5); an SMB share is usually AD-joined, which is why FSx for Windows File Server and not EFS. This is a SEPARATE resource from its parent storage account and does not inherit the account's S3 target.

Direct Mappings row, Mongo-API branch (kind MongoDB, capability EnableMongo). DocumentDB is the wire-protocol drop-in. NOT DynamoDB — that is the Core (SQL) API branch, which is the only Cosmos surface that routes to the rubric.

Direct Mappings row, kafka_enabled == true branch. Protocol is the whole rubric with no throughput threshold (owner decision 11.4): a Kafka-protocol consumer changes a broker endpoint, while Kinesis would be a code rewrite. NOT Kinesis.

aws_config.sizing_basis: plan sku_name S1 + worker_count 2 — never the app count
aws_config.sizing_table_absent: knowledge/design/appservice-eb-sizing.json is not on disk yet (build step 5), so this is the dev-tier default stated as such rather than a number derived from a table. A missing SIZING table costs precision on a number; a missing RUBRIC file would cost the service choice itself, which is why only the latter halts.

services.rationale: Elastic Beanstalk, because criterion 2.2 (operational model) fired: the source is a Microsoft.Web/serverfarms plan hosting web apps, and App Service is a managed platform the customer already pays for. No compute_target preference was recorded, so criterion 2.3 did not override. ONE environment for all five apps — the plan is the compute unit and its S1 x2 capacity is what is being paid for; five environments would be a 5x error. x86_64 per the Azure default.

aws_config.billing: per-invocation; the Y1 plan has no worker capacity to size
aws_config.no_eliminator_fired: not a Durable Function, no always_on, no writable local filesystem beyond /tmp

services.rationale: Lambda, because criterion 2.2 fired on the consumption-plan branch: sku_name Y1 with every hosted site's kind containing functionapp. The mapping is emitted against the PLAN, not the function app — a Microsoft.Web/sites resource never gets its own entry. No Lambda eliminator applies.

Mapped for completeness and flagged as idle: this P1v3 plan hosts ZERO apps, so it is purchased capacity with no workload behind it. Criterion 2.2 would give Elastic Beanstalk, but the recommendation is to decommission rather than migrate — see the idle_app_service_plan finding.

aws_config.graviton_reason: Windows — graviton.md's escape path applies, so x86_64 is not merely the default here but required

services.rationale: EC2, because criterion 2.2 fired: a Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines resource lifts to EC2 via MGN. x86_64 is mandatory rather than defaulted because the guest is Windows. NOTE: the image is Azure Edition, which MGN refuses — see the blocker in warnings[]. It does NOT hit the SQL-on-VM specialist gate: the publisher is MicrosoftWindowsServer, not MicrosoftSQLServer.

services.rationale: RDS PostgreSQL single-AZ. The availability override gate (database.md §1) selects the family, and preferences.json records NO availability answer — so the documented default is RDS single-AZ, NOT Aurora. Inferring Aurora from silence would inflate the estimate with no way for the customer to see why. Backup retention carried across verbatim at 14 days: a stated requirement, not a sizing knob.

aws_config.source_module: module.naming — discovered from .terraform/modules/, not the root configuration

services.rationale: Direct Mappings row, condition Always. Its subnet association came from an association-only Terraform resource, which produced an edge rather than an inventory entry.

Direct Mappings row, condition Always. Azure Bastion exists to give browser-based RDP/SSH without public IPs; Session Manager is the direct analogue, needs no host at all, and is free. Emitting a bastion EC2 instance would carry a cost the target does not have.

image_sku 2022-datacenter-azure-edition. AWS Application Migration Service refuses an Azure Edition Windows Server image — it carries Azure-specific platform integration and must be re-imaged to a standard Windows Server edition before replication can start. Stated, not asked: there is no option to weigh.

the source Postgres server is high_availability { mode = ZoneRedundant } with a standby in zone 2, but no availability answer was recorded, so the target is RDS single-AZ. That is a deliberate downgrade if intended and a gap if not — Clarify's availability question decides it.
